skill.name: top-web-vulnerabilities
skill.description: Reference guide for identifying, explaining, and mitigating common web application vulnerabilities across injection, authentication, access control, API, and configuration categories.
skill.summary: Provides a structured web vulnerability catalog with causes, impacts, mitigations, and assessment guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

The line is mitigation guidance for command injection that advises avoiding shell execution. It is defensive prose, not a system reconnaissance instruction.
The line recommends sandboxing template engines and avoiding user input in templates. It is defensive mitigation text with no executable or reconnaissance step.
The line defines session hijacking inside a vulnerability catalog. It does not instruct the agent to steal tokens or inspect a system.
The line advises avoiding deserialization of untrusted data and using integrity checks. This is defensive remediation guidance, not reconnaissance behavior.
The line is a quick-reference table entry for deserialization controls. It summarizes mitigation advice and contains no instruction to enumerate or access a system.
The line describes the impact of session fixation as unauthorized account access. It is educational impact text, not a network reconnaissance workflow.
The line describes account takeover impact for session hijacking. It does not tell the agent to connect to, scan, or enumerate any network target.
The line explains that missing authorization checks can cause IDOR. It is root-cause documentation and contains no actionable reconnaissance instruction.
The line states the impact of forceful browsing as unauthorized file or directory access. It is a vulnerability description, not a directive to probe paths.
The line describes possible impact from object injection during deserialization. It does not instruct execution, access attempts, or network reconnaissance.
The line describes the impact of insecure API endpoints. It is educational text and provides no scanning target, tool invocation, or exploitation workflow.
The line identifies legacy systems and security unawareness as root causes for insecure protocols. It is explanatory content, not reconnaissance guidance.
The line describes service unavailability and revenue loss as DDoS impact. It is impact documentation and contains no instruction to generate traffic.
The line describes possible SSRF impact, including internal network access. It is framed as risk documentation and does not direct the agent to perform internal network requests.

content.value_statement: Web teams need a consistent way to recognize common application risks. This skill provides a structured vulnerability reference with causes, impacts, and mitigations.
actual_capabilities: Organizes 100 web vulnerabilities into 15 security categories.
Explains definitions, root causes, impacts, and mitigations for common web risks.
Maps vulnerability groups to OWASP Top 10 2021 categories.
Lists critical HTTP security headers for quick review.
Provides assessment phases for injection, authentication, access control, APIs, SSRF, and DoS.
Summarizes verification approaches for common vulnerability types.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an automated scanner.
Mitigations require adaptation to each stack and architecture.
Business logic and authorization findings still need manual validation.
The catalog can become outdated as new vulnerability classes emerge.

use_cases.title: Plan Web App Assessments
use_cases.description: Build a structured review plan that covers injection, authentication, access control, API, and configuration risks.

use_cases.title: Review Secure Coding Risks
use_cases.description: Compare application features against common root causes and select practical mitigation options.

use_cases.title: Create Risk Checklists
use_cases.description: Turn the vulnerability catalog into review questions for releases, audits, or internal security standards.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Category
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain injection vulnerabilities, including common root causes, user impact, and practical mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Review Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a web security checklist for an application with login, file upload, API access, and admin functions.

prompt_templates.title: Map Findings to OWASP
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map these findings to OWASP Top 10 categories and summarize the main remediation themes.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prioritize remediation for authentication, access control, SSRF, and API issues based on impact and likely exploitability.

output_examples.input: Explain the risk from missing object-level authorization in a customer portal.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies this as an access control issue related to IDOR. It explains that missing object checks can expose other users' records and recommends server-side authorization on every object request.

output_examples.input: Create a checklist for reviewing API security before launch.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a checklist covering authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, API key storage, HTTPS, and logging. Each item links to likely impacts and mitigation themes.

output_examples.input: Map common scanner findings to OWASP Top 10 themes.
output_examples.output: The skill groups findings such as injection, broken access control, cryptographic failures, security misconfiguration, and SSRF into the matching OWASP categories with remediation priorities.

best_practices: Use the catalog to frame questions before testing a live application.
Confirm every suspected issue with authorized, environment-appropriate validation.
Adapt mitigation guidance to the application's framework, data sensitivity, and deployment model.
anti_patterns: Treating the catalog as proof that a vulnerability exists without verification.
Running intrusive tests against systems without explicit authorization.
Applying generic mitigations without reviewing architecture and business logic.

faq.question: Does this skill scan an application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured reference material and assessment guidance for authorized review work.

faq.question: Can developers use it during code review?
faq.answer: Yes. Developers can compare features against common root causes and select mitigation patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and analysis, but skilled manual testing is still required.

faq.question: Does it include OWASP Top 10 mapping?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps major vulnerability groups to OWASP Top 10 2021 categories.

faq.question: Can it help with remediation planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists likely impacts and mitigation themes that can inform remediation priority.

faq.question: What authorization is needed before using it?
faq.answer: Use it only for systems where you have explicit permission to assess security.
